Many years ago, MacBooks included a slot that worked with a cable lock to secure the computer to a table leg or similar fixed object. These accessories were handy when you wanted to leave your laptop behind at a coffee shop while you headed back to the counter for another drink.

Those slots disappeared long ago, but adapters are now available to add a security lock to the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro...

If you remember the recessed security slot on the side of a MacBook, you’re likely a pretty long-time MacBook user. Those slots were designed for a T-shaped accessory that you would slide into the slot and then rotate 90 degrees to lock it into place. The most common design featured a steel cable that could thread through a table leg, popular in coffee shops or libraries.

CompuLock is now bringing the idea back with an adapter that mounts to the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version to the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It must be stressed that locks like these have always only been a very low level of security, only meant to deter someone from grabbing your MacBook and running off during the few seconds you might be distracted. I felt comfortable using one in a smaller coffee shop where I could still see my table while ordering another tea at the counter, but would never let my MacBook out of my sight relying on it alone.

The adapter costs $70, which isn’t cheap, and you still need to buy the lock itself separately; but if you happen to have an old lock in your drawer, it might be worth bringing it back into service.
